title: Doc drill 18.1.1
prompt: Elaborate on the meaning of time management.
marking_points: Time management is the skill of using time in the most productive way in order to complete assigned tasks.
It is also the ability to manage time effectively, using the number of hours available in the day to work towards important goals.
Effective time management means that less time is wasted, which results in deadlines being met timeously and a reduction of unnecessary stress.
It also promotes self-discipline and enables one to complete set tasks on time.
sample_answer: Time management is the skill of using time productively to complete assigned tasks and work towards important goals. It reduces wasted time, helps meet deadlines timeously, lowers stress and promotes self-discipline.
explanation: Time management is using available hours effectively to reach goals, meet deadlines and reduce stress.
guidelines: Refer to Self-management, Unit 18.1 in the curriculum document.

title: Doc drill 18.2.1.1
prompt: Explain the importance of recognising one's strengths and weaknesses.
marking_points: It is important to conduct a SWOT analysis to make use of strengths and minimise weaknesses and threats while taking advantage of opportunities.
You can work to improve on your weaknesses once you can recognise them.
Concentrate on your strengths as much as possible.
Improve the weaknesses that could potentially harm your life or career.
Build on strengths and learn to manage your weaknesses.
Surround yourself with people who can uplift you instead of those who choose not to change.
sample_answer: Recognising strengths and weaknesses allows a SWOT analysis, helps improve weaknesses, build on strengths and manage the weaknesses that could harm one's life or career.
explanation: Self-awareness through identifying strengths and weaknesses guides personal improvement.
guidelines: Refer to Self-management, Activity 18.1 in the curriculum document.

title: Doc drill 18.2.1.2
prompt: Suggest ways to build one's strengths and weaknesses.
marking_points: Identify your strengths before you consider your weaknesses.
Focus on taking full advantage of your strengths rather than investing scarce resources in correcting weaknesses.
Develop your skills to the maximum and push your talents as far as you can.
Talent in a particular area should not be ignored; time should rather be spent enhancing it.
Break your weaknesses into those you can change by setting goals and those you cannot change and must manage.
sample_answer: Identify and build on strengths, develop talents to the maximum, and break weaknesses into those that can be changed through goal setting and those that must simply be managed.
explanation: Building strengths and managing weaknesses maximises personal potential.
guidelines: Refer to Self-management, Activity 18.1 in the curriculum document.

title: Doc drill 18.2.2
prompt: Discuss the importance of setting goals.
marking_points: Goal setting helps you to organise your time and resources so that you live a productive and satisfying life.
Setting goals gives long-term vision and short-term motivation.
When setting goals you take control of your life and have direction of where you want to go.
You can create an action plan and review it even when things are not on track.
Goals give you focus because you spend your time and energy achieving exactly what you want.
Goals enable you to achieve your highest potential because you set targets to strive towards.
sample_answer: Setting goals organises time and resources, provides vision and motivation, gives direction and focus, allows action plans to be reviewed, and helps one reach their highest potential.
explanation: Goals provide direction, motivation and focus for a productive life.
guidelines: Refer to Self-management, Activity 18.1 in the curriculum document.

title: Doc drill 18.3.1.1
prompt: Elaborate on the meaning of self-management.
marking_points: Self-management skills are the abilities that allow people to control their thoughts, feelings and actions.
People with strong self-management skills can set goals independently and take the initiative to achieve them.
sample_answer: Self-management is the ability to control one's thoughts, feelings and actions, set goals independently and take the initiative to achieve them.
explanation: Self-management is regulating one's own behaviour and taking initiative toward goals.
guidelines: Refer to Self-management, Unit 18.2 in the curriculum document.

title: Doc drill 18.3.1.2
prompt: Recommend ways in which people can adapt to change.
marking_points: People should adapt their learning styles and skills to make the most of new learning opportunities.
They should transfer and adapt skills and resources for new tasks and situations.
Avoid complaining and learn to be positive about change.
Find ways to meet the challenges that change brings and benefit from them.
Be proactive by keeping up with changes taking place in the world.
Accept that change is inevitable and take responsibility to respond to it.
sample_answer: Adapt to change by adjusting learning styles, transferring skills, staying positive, meeting challenges, being proactive, and accepting that change is inevitable while taking responsibility to respond.
explanation: Adaptability is adjusting actions and attitudes to suit new situations.
guidelines: Refer to Self-management, Activity 18.2 in the curriculum document.

title: Doc drill 18.4.1.2
prompt: Outline the importance of a professional image.
marking_points: It creates an impression on others.
People form ideas about who you are and what you are capable of.
If you are aware of the image you project, you can influence how others see you.
Being viewed positively has huge benefits for your career, work relationships and work experience.
The image a business projects helps build customer confidence.
Companies providing both a professional image and quality service attract and retain customers.
sample_answer: A professional image creates impressions, influences how others see you, benefits career and work relationships, builds customer confidence and helps businesses attract and retain customers.
explanation: Professional image shapes perceptions and builds confidence with employers and customers.
guidelines: Refer to Self-management, Consolidation Question 1 in the curriculum document.

title: Doc drill 18.4.2.1
marking_points: Set aside personal time.
Develop a healthy lifestyle.
Spend time with people you enjoy or love.
Have a plan so that you stay in control.
Exercise regularly and take a break.
Reduce caffeine intake and eat a well-balanced diet.
Be assertive, be optimistic and have a sense of humour.
sample_answer: Manage stress by setting aside personal time, living healthily, exercising, planning, eating well, reducing caffeine, and staying assertive, optimistic and good-humoured.
explanation: Stress management involves lifestyle, planning and attitude changes.
guidelines: Refer to Self-management, Consolidation Question 2 in the curriculum document.

title: Doc drill 18.4.2.3
prompt: Suggest other ways in which a business can encourage employees to live a successful and balanced lifestyle.
marking_points: Encourage employees to maintain a positive attitude and take responsibility for their actions.
Engage employees in self-development programmes to enhance growth.
Promote proper hygiene and regular physical exercise.
Physical wellbeing: enough exercise and rest and a healthy, balanced diet.
Mental wellbeing: planning the day and activities to avoid unnecessary stress.
Spiritual wellbeing: making time for the religion one practises.
Social wellbeing: doing good deeds by giving, helping and guiding others.
sample_answer: A business can encourage balance through a positive attitude, self-development, hygiene and exercise, and attention to physical, mental, spiritual and social wellbeing.
explanation: A balanced lifestyle covers physical, mental, spiritual and social wellbeing.
guidelines: Refer to Self-management, Consolidation Question 2 in the curriculum document.

title: Doc MCQ 18.4.1.1.1
prompt: The term that is the ability to turn understanding, acceptance and love inward is:
marking_points: self-compassion
explanation: Memo: self-compassion is the ability to turn understanding, acceptance and love inward.
guidelines: Authentic CAPS question from the Self-management curriculum document.

title: Doc MCQ 18.4.1.1.2
prompt: The skills that allow people to control their thoughts, feelings and actions are the:
marking_points: self-management
explanation: Memo: self-management skills are the abilities that allow people to control their thoughts, feelings and actions.
guidelines: Authentic CAPS question from the Self-management curriculum document.
